title: Risk first, invest second, option overlays third
summary: At his former hedge fund, clients chose a benchmark for beta exposure and the fund added relative-value derivative trades for alpha. Individuals can do the same: hold core beta with shares, ETFs or, his preference, 95-delta calls, and add option overlays on top.

steps.caption: The bar is the portfolio. The order is risk first, invest second, overlays third.
Step 1, risk: decide the most you can lose before choosing positions.
Step 2, core beta: shares, ETFs or 95-delta calls that track a chosen benchmark.
Step 3, overlays: option trades on top of the core aim to add alpha.
Cash holds the rest and funds the overlays.
Same structure as the hedge fund: a benchmark for beta plus relative-value trades for alpha.

takeaways: Separate beta (the core benchmark exposure) from alpha (overlay trades).
The speaker uses shares, ETFs or 95-delta calls for the core.
Define risk first, invest second, add option overlays third.
caveats: The allocation split is illustrative; the speaker gives no percentages.
Hedge-fund background is the speaker's own claim.
